div.br:
• User is abstract: there is no "generic user", only the five concrete roles.
• getRole() is polymorphic: each subclass overrides it and Spring Security decides the permissions with that value.
• Teacher and ExternalEvaluator grade groups but have no parent of their own for that: the shared behavior is the Evaluator interface, and each one implements its own canEvaluate() rule (the teacher who enabled the group, the evaluators assigned to it).
• Business person, alumnus and the types created later are rows of the EvaluatorType catalog, not classes (ADR-011).
• Student, Admin and SuperAdmin do not grade, so they do not implement Evaluator: there is no self-assessment.
• JPA maps the inheritance with @Inheritance(JOINED): an app_user table plus one table per role (ADR-009).

div.div:
Each moment has its own RAP, criteria and levels with scores, defined by the admin in each academic period; nothing is fixed in the code (ADR-010).
The final grade is a weighted average by kind of evaluator (the teacher and each EvaluatorType), with the weights the admin sets in each moment.

div.div: Filtering is applied in the service layer (AccessScope and the rules of each service), not in the user interface. A teacher only sees and grades the groups they enabled; an admin only manages their faculty; students see every group of the moment of their semester to join one, and then only their own group; external evaluators only see and grade the groups assigned to them.
